classification.difficultyReason: Identify standard-deviation intervals and combine or halve empirical-rule percentages, including asymmetric intervals.

content.prompt:
A set of data is normally distributed with mean 18 and standard deviation 2.

Find the percentage of data between:

answer.worked:
$16=18-2$ and $20=18+2$, so the interval is $-1\le z\le1$.

By the empirical rule, approximately $68\%$ of the data lies in this interval.

$14=18-2(2)$ and $22=18+2(2)$, so the interval is $-2\le z\le2$.

By the empirical rule, approximately $95\%$ of the data lies in this interval.

$12=18-3(2)$ and $24=18+3(2)$, so the interval is $-3\le z\le3$.

By the empirical rule, approximately $99.7\%$ of the data lies in this interval.

$16=18-2$, so the interval is $-1\le z\le0$.

By symmetry, the percentage is approximately $68\%\div2=34\%$.

$24=18+3(2)$, so the interval is $0\le z\le3$.

By symmetry, the percentage is approximately $99.7\%\div2=49.85\%$.

$12=18-3(2)$ and $22=18+2(2)$, so the interval is $-3\le z\le2$.

The percentage is approximately
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{99.7\%}{2}+\frac{95\%}{2}&=49.85\%+47.5\%\\&=97.35\%.\end{aligned}$$
